MEASUREMENT_STATUS: ESTIMATED - see module docstring. Not a live measurement.

cost_levers.tool_block_size: The system prompt's tool descriptors are resent on EVERY turn (see prompt.py / prompt.audit()). A longer descriptor block multiplies its cost by the number of turns in every run, not just once - measured in characters/~tokens via `run_eval.py --prompt`.
cost_levers.turn_count: Each turn re-sends the growing transcript, so cost grows roughly with T (turns) and, for the base prompt prefix, with T again - see D2(c)'s parallel-vs-sequential result (results/parallelism/comparison.json): grouping independent calls into fewer turns is a direct token saving, not just a latency one.
cost_levers.observation_size: Tool observations are appended to the transcript and re-sent every subsequent turn. get_clinic_slots can return many rows; trimming or summarising large observations before they re-enter the transcript is a lever this project's tools do not yet exploit.
cost_levers.success_rate: Dominates the fallback term (see the sensitivity note above) once fallback cost per failure (US$9.17) is much larger than the per-referral model cost - true at this dataset's scale, and the reason chasing success rate matters more than shaving tokens once a model is already cheap.

next_step: Re-run this script unchanged once results/live/model_comparison.json exists (D5b) - swap the ESTIMATE line for the measured mean cost and the ILLUSTRATIVE success rates for the measured pass rate.

measured_one_model.MEASUREMENT_STATUS: REAL measured numbers (one model, one prompt version) - not the full D5b family comparison.
measured_one_model.success_rate_caveat: This is the D4 CODE-CHECK pass rate over 107 evaluation trials on the CURRENT 45-case, 69%-negative eval set, for the v2 prompt - not yet a large-sample production success rate, and not the number for every prompt: the SAME model with the deliberately worse v1 prompt scores only 27.1% on the identical trials (results/descriptors/comparison.json) - a much larger gap than on the earlier, mostly-positive 35-case set (45.5%), because this set is dominated by cases needing an EXACT trigger/missing label, which v1's schema cannot supply even when it reaches the right underlying decision. v2's 2 residual failures are non-reproducible flakes, not a systematic gap - see docs/D4_EVALUATION.md and STATUS.md.

measured_all_models_note: 5-model D5(b) battery, all on the identical 45-case/107-trial v2-prompt eval set, real OpenRouter usage. Cheapest at this scale (4000 referrals/month) is openai/gpt-4o-mini at $10.80/month, driven almost entirely by its 100.0% success rate keeping the fallback term small - not by having the lowest raw per-token price. A model with a lower sticker price but a materially lower success rate (e.g. mistralai/mistral-nemo or meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct, both <40% pass) costs far more overall once the $9.17/failure fallback is priced in.
